speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Cutaneous Leishmaniasis. The combination of a leg ulcer with a history of trauma/insect bite, your immunocompromised state (Crohn's, diabetes, steroid use), and the chronic one-month duration strongly suggests this parasitic infection. I am awaiting your photographic images of the lesion to confirm the specific morphology before initiating treatment.
